article_title: Chai Discovery Raises $400 Million Series C at $3.8 Billion Valuation as Pfizer, Lilly and Novartis Deals Pile Up
summary: Core facts (funding amount, valuation, investors, pharma partnerships) verified against all 3 cited sources; two body-paragraph quote/attribution errors found and documented in a corrections record. Headline, summary, and lead are fully supported.

findings.message: Quote misattributed to SiliconANGLE; actually from BioSpace
findings.details: The sentence 'The company's Chai-2 model, released in 2025, was "the first zero-shot generative platform for fully de novo antibody design to achieve double-digit experimental success rates," according to [SiliconANGLE]' cites the SiliconANGLE article, but this exact phrase does not appear anywhere in the SiliconANGLE snapshot (source-0). It appears verbatim in the BioSpace $400M Series C press release (source-1): 'Chai-2, released in 2025, was the first zero-shot generative platform for fully de novo antibody design to achieve double-digit experimental success rates.' The quote itself is accurate and verbatim, just attributed to the wrong outlet. Similarly, part of the extended investor list ('Glade Brook, Avenir, Lachy Groom and Yosemite') attributed solely to SiliconANGLE in the same paragraph is only found in the BioSpace source (source-0/SiliconANGLE names only Thrive Capital, OpenAI, Oak HC/FT, Menlo Ventures and General Catalyst as existing investors, 'among others').

findings.message: Paraphrased text presented in quotation marks; one specific date not supported by source
findings.details: The sentence describing the Novartis collaboration timeline reads: 'The agreement "extends work that began over a year prior, including early access to Chai's next-generation folding model in spring 2025," the outlet reported.' The BioSpace Novartis release (source-2) actually says: 'The agreement builds on more than a year of technical engagement between the two companies, including early access to Chai's next-generation folding model last spring.' This is a paraphrase, not a verbatim quote, and the source never specifies a year for 'last spring' — since the release is dated July 13, 2026, 'last spring' most plausibly means spring 2026, not spring 2025 as the article states. The specific year '2025' appears to be a bot-added inference presented inside quotation marks as if sourced, and is more likely incorrect than correct given the publication date. A separate sentence in the same paragraph ('gains access to Chai Discovery's AI models to support therapeutic antibody discovery across multiple targets') is also a loose paraphrase of the source's subheading ('will gain access to Chai Discovery's AI design models and platform...') rather than a verbatim quote.

content_preview.title: Chai Discovery Raises $400 Million Series C at $3.8 Billion Valuation as Pfizer, Lilly and Novartis Deals Pile Up
content_preview.summary: AI drug-design startup Chai Discovery raised $400 million at a $3.8 billion valuation, nearly tripling its worth in seven months as Pfizer, Eli Lilly and Novartis sign on.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Chai Discovery, a San Francisco startup that builds AI models for molecular design, has raised $400 million in a Series C round that values the company at $3.8 billion, according to [SiliconANGLE](https://siliconangle.com/2026/07/14/chai-discovery-nabs-400m-series-c-ai-designed-antibodies-reach-big-pharma/). The round was led by Index Ventures, with Kleiner Perkins, Sequoia Capital and Dimension co-leading, according to [BioSpace](https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/chai-discove...

recommendations: When a single fact or figure is corroborated by multiple press-release sources, cite the outlet that actually contains the exact wording used, not the outlet cited earlier in the same paragraph.
Do not present paraphrased sentences inside quotation marks; either quote verbatim or drop the quote marks and attribute the paraphrase in prose.
Do not infer or add a specific year/date that a source states only in relative terms (e.g. 'last spring') without independently confirming it.

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know) at 572 words, within the 400-1200 word News range. Clear, neutral, informative prose with appropriate technical context on antibody design and industry-wide AI drug discovery stats.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 3 cited sources were fetched successfully (HTTP 200) and their local gzip snapshots verified: source-0.html.gz (SiliconANGLE, sha256 b39c9df...11f5bd, matches manifest), source-1.html.gz (BioSpace $400M Series C release, sha256 3010fc7...857a3a, matches manifest), source-2.html.gz (BioSpace Novartis collaboration release, sha256 635536e...989bf3d, matches manifest). Read full extracted text of all three. Core facts -- $400M raise, $3.8B valuation (nearly tripling the $1.3B December 2025 mark), Index Ventures-led round with Kleiner Perkins/Sequoia/Dimension, the full investor roster, the Meier CEO quote, the Pfizer licensing deal, the Eli Lilly customer agreement, the Novartis collaboration announcement, Fiona Marshall's quote, the Meier Novartis quote, undisclosed financial terms, the $20B industry investment figure and 173 AI-originated drug programs figure (both correctly sub-attributed to Excelra Knowledge Solutions and OncoDaily via SiliconANGLE) -- all check out against the snapshots. Two attribution/quote-fidelity issues found in the body (not headline/summary/lead), documented in findings above and filed as a corrections record: (1) the Chai-2 'zero-shot generative platform' quote and part of the extended investor list are attributed to SiliconANGLE but actually appear only in the BioSpace release; (2) the Novartis-collaboration timeline sentence paraphrases the BioSpace release while presented in quotation marks, and adds an unsupported/likely-incorrect year ('spring 2025' vs. the source's undated 'last spring', which — given the source's July 13, 2026 publish date — more plausibly means spring 2026).
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: No fabricated events, no invented sources, no bidirectional source-array gap (all 3 body URLs match article.sources exactly). The headline, summary, and Overview lead paragraph are each fully supported by the cited sources with no material errors. The two issues found are confined to secondary paragraphs in the body: a source-attribution mix-up (the underlying facts are true and appear in the article's own other cited source) and a paraphrase-as-quote with one likely-incorrect year. Neither issue changes the article's central thesis (a large up-round for an AI drug-design startup with growing pharma traction).
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout. No sensationalism, no editorializing, no AI self-reference. Appropriately hedges what is not yet known (clinical trial status, financial terms) in a dedicated 'What We Don't Know' section.
editor_notes.originality: Searched src/content/articles/ for prior 'Chai Discovery' coverage -- none found. This is a new topic, not a duplicate or rehash of existing Machine Herald coverage.
concerns: Quote attributed to SiliconANGLE ('the first zero-shot generative platform...') actually originates from the BioSpace $400M release; part of the extended investor list has the same issue.

Novartis-collaboration paragraph presents paraphrased BioSpace text in quotation marks and states 'spring 2025' for a folding-model access date the source only describes as 'last spring' (undated, and likely spring 2026 given the source's July 2026 publish date).
recommendations: File a corrections record documenting both attribution issues per the APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS workflow.
Future submissions should double check which specific outlet's snapshot contains the exact wording being quoted, especially when multiple sources cover overlapping facts.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively strong, accurately sourced article on a genuinely new topic. Headline, summary, and lead are solid. Two recoverable body-paragraph issues (source misattribution for an otherwise-true quote/list, and a paraphrase-as-quote with a likely-incorrect year) do not gut the article's thesis and can be honestly summarized in a public corrections note. Verdict: APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS.
